conviction_note: The bar ($59.0m revenue, $0.09 EPS) is an 11% sequential drop from Q4's $66.2m. Against it stand three things: backlog of $164.4m, up 22.5% year on year with 'faster turns' (company deck, 26 Aug); semi-equipment peers that reported after RELL last spoke and printed records or raised guides; and a name that has bought its beats (+21%, +23%) while carrying a 9% short. So p_up is 60, a lean built on a proxy plus a public company number, on a 15% absolute move. That gives +3.0 scaled against an impact_sum of +4.8. The gap is the uncertainty kept in p_up: management gave no Q1 guide and says backlog does not convert linearly.
bar: Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 2026-08-29). EPS $0.09: MarketBeat consensus https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/RELL/earnings/ and EarningsWhispers https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/RELL agree; Northland cut its estimate to $0.09 from $0.11 and Sidoti is at $0.10 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/what-is-northland-securities-estimate-for-rell-q1-earnings-2026-07-29/). Revenue $58.99m per EarningsWhispers; a second aggregator snippet gives $58.5m. Two roughly agreeing sources, so no cap. There is no company guide, so nothing lands inside a guided range.
positioning_check: Short interest 925,687 shares, 9.22% of float, 9.0 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-15, up 6.6% from 868,020 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/RELL/short-interest/). Skew is -1.72 vol points (25d calls slightly richer than puts) and put/call OI 0.28, so the option market leans mildly toward upside. The event-implied move is 13.08%. The stock has run up 8.3% over 20 days and sits 13.5% below its 52-week high of about $21.8, which it reached in early August after the Q4 print.

findings.finding: Semi-equipment counterparties printed after RELL last spoke on 22-23 July, and every one accelerated in RELL's June-August quarter. Advanced Energy: record semi revenue of $278m, +27% q/q (3 Aug). MKS: beat above the top of its guide (5 Aug). Applied Materials: record $9.12bn and a fourth-quarter guide of $10.25bn against $9.54bn expected (13 Aug). Tokyo Electron: +33% y/y (26 Aug). Yet the street bar has RELL revenue falling 11% sequentially, and wafer fab is the stated growth driver of PMT, which is 72% of RELL sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PMT wafer-fab strength drove Q4 FY26 (PMT +28.1%, revenue $66.2m vs $55.4m est.), and the stock moved +21.15% on 2026-07-22. Q3 FY26 (revenue $55.5m vs $53.1m) moved +22.7%. A revenue miss in Q3 FY25 moved -17.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts cut the Q1 estimate after the Q4 beat (Northland $0.11 to $0.09, 29 July), before any of these peer prints, and no estimate change since has been found. Had the peer read-through been priced, the consensus revenue bar would sit near Q4's run-rate rather than at $59m. The stock would also be near its August high rather than 13.5% below it.
findings.independence: Advanced Energy Q2 2026 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000927003/000092700326000030/aeis-20260803xex99d1.htm (2026-08-03); TEL Q1 FY2027, https://www.rttnews.com/3672872/tokyo-electron-q1-net-income-rises.aspx. All are proxies: RELL itself said on 23 July only that customer feedback was 'very, very positive' and should continue through FY27 (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/RELL/Q42026). The rest of the company (Canvys, GES) points the same way, so there is no offsetting segment. This finding overlaps finding 2, because PMT backlog growth is partly this same demand, and it was trimmed for that.

findings.finding: Year-end backlog was $164.4m, +22.5% y/y and +8.7% q/q, the highest in three years. The company's 26 August investor deck adds that the 'current backlog also includes faster turns than prior years'. Canvys entered Q1 with a 1.3 book-to-bill and record backlog. The $59m bar implies only +8% y/y revenue on a backlog up 22.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog and sales growth have been the line this name trades on: +21.15% (2026-07-22) and +22.7% (2026-04-08) on quarters with backlog growth and revenue beats; -11.73% (2026-01-07) on an in-line EPS quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline backlog is in the wire, but the 'faster turns' remark sits only in a conference deck that no aggregator carries. The bar was set at a sequential decline despite it. If the market had read backlog as convertible, the Q1 estimate would not have been cut after a $0.14 EPS beat.
findings.independence: Q4 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000355948/000119312526312436/rell-ex99_1.htm (2026-07-22), which gives the same $164.4m figure, so this is the same company source. Caveat applied: management also said 'backlog does not convert to revenue linearly' (https://stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/RELL/2026/Q4), which is why the size is held at 2.0 rather than larger.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 6.6% into the print to 9.22% of float with 9.0 days to cover on a name trading about 123k shares a day. Combined with this name's history of buying beats (+21%, +23% on the last two), a beat has a squeeze mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two upside prints moved +21% and +23%, above the 13.1% implied move. Shorts have been squeezed hard on beats.
findings.why_not_priced: The option market prices a 13.1% move with only a mild call bid (-1.72 skew). If the squeeze were priced, the implied move would be nearer the last two realised moves (21-23%) and calls would carry a clearer premium.
findings.independence: The baseline's options block (skew -1.72, put/call OI 0.28) points the same way. It comes from a different source but reflects the same crowd.

findings.finding: A cluster of at least nine insiders sold after the July print, between 28 July and 20 August, at $17.90-21.61, much of it option exercise-and-sell. Sellers included the COO (23,901 shares at $20.00), the CFO (two sales), the EVP of Canvys (37,500 shares) and several directors, and some of the selling came late in the quarter now being reported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance found to compare against.
findings.why_not_priced: The Form 4s are public, so this is largely priced. It is a weak tell at most, because the sales are routine post-window option monetisation.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list shows Form 4s and Form 144s from 22 July to 24 August (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000355948&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). It is the same set of filings. Shrunk from -0.8 because of the 9% short interest and 9 days to cover.

findings.finding: Management promised on 23 July a multi-million-dollar BES order in Q1, and it was announced on 20 August: the Alaska program, 18 systems, 7 MWh. Deliveries run through end-2027, so it adds to GES backlog and adds little to Q1 revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance found to compare against.
findings.why_not_priced: The order itself is public. What is not yet visible is its effect on the Q1 backlog figure, which the release will show.

rejected_candidates.candidate: RELL paid about $16m of IEEPA tariffs in 2025 and sued for a refund in December 2025, which would land as a one-off gain
rejected_candidates.detail: The search-snippet attribution appears to mix in another issuer (CIK 106532). RELL's FY2026 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000355948/000035594826000002/rell-20260530.htm) contains no IEEPA, refund or CIT disclosure and says the tariff modifications did not materially impact FY26 results.

rejected_candidates.candidate: An aggregator said the earnings date is 21 October 2026
rejected_candidates.detail: The company's own date release confirms 7 October after the close, with the call on 8 October.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A press snippet said the stock edged down 0.3% after the Q4 FY26 print
rejected_candidates.detail: The sealed baseline's bars show +21.15% for the 22 July event, and insider sales at $18.6-21.6 in the following days are consistent with that.

baseline_tension: The findings agree with the mild call skew and the +8% 20-day run-up, so part of this is priced. But the stock is still 13.5% below its August high, and the consensus revenue bar sits below Q4's run-rate, so the agreement is partial rather than full.
lessons_applied: Rules 3 and 5 plus the duplicate check: the peer-WFE proxy finding was trimmed from +2.5 to +2.0, because RELL's own backlog (finding 2) already embodies part of the same demand.
Rule 7: the insider-selling negative was shrunk from -0.8 to -0.5 because of 9.2% short interest and 9.0 days to cover.
Rule 8: on thin coverage (two analysts) with the last two moves at 21-23%, abs_move_pct was raised from 14 to 15.
Rules 1, 6 and 9 left the set standing: this name has bought its beats; the bar has two agreeing sources; the non-PMT segments (Canvys book-to-bill 1.3, GES backlog +5%) do not offset.
